newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha firm, S Korea still offering Aug LSWR.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha firm, S Korea still offering Aug LSWR.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha was firmer in afternoon trade on Tuesday, buoyed by an overseas crude oil rally, but the naphtha gains were proportionally smaller than those of crude oil due to slack prompt demand, traders said.

Naphtha prices in Asia normally follow crude oil's lead in New York and London, and the price movements of naphtha, traded by tonne, are usually seven to nine times larger than the price fluctuations of crude oil, traded by barrel, traders said.
Asia's benchmark forward contract open-spec naphtha gained only about by $1.50 per tonne on Tuesday, although overnight crude oil prices had shot up about 50 cents a barrel.
Second-half October open-spec naphtha was assessed at $211.50/213.50. A South Korean trader was said to have bought the contract at $211.00 on Monday.

A South Korean refiner said it was still offering a 200,000 to 300,000 barrels of low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) for August. A trader with the oil firm said he was negotiating with some of the Japanese oil firms.

He said he was offering the straight-run cargo, processed from Daqing crude oil, at about $1.50 per barrel over the mean of Singapore quotes on a FOB (free on board) basis, or at a $2.90 to $3.00 premium on a C&F (cost and freight) Japan basis.
